label: D-99246e

defects.summary: The unconfined caveat shown for every unconfined row is rewritten in both halves, from 'a shell is always there' to 'its tools reach past what it is given' (also in AdmissionFlags.Caveat, capabilityAdmission.ts, CapabilityStanding's doc and the seed header); this changes text that codex and other rows show too, no story decision asks for it, and deviations 50–59 do not record it.
The new caveat test cites 'R2' as its reason, but R2 in the plan is E5.3's lock-order rule, so the citation points nowhere true.

The status line and the as-built heading say E5.5–E5.6 were built on Sonnet, but §0/§0.2 mark both stories for Opus; the change is not recorded as a deviation, so either the line is untrue or the deviation is missing.

TheVectorsCoverKimi copies the existing TheVectorsActuallyLoaded_AndCoverEveryPairOfTheTable, which the spec names as S5.6.2, and deviation 53's reason is weak: with kimi in both the seed and Runtimes but no vectors, the existing test already goes red as the table says.
The new shared stand-in copies the private StandIn of AKimiConsultationScenarioTests (without CallingAs), and the old class is not changed to use it.
MustCarryNoFlag checks only Leading and Flags, so a hand-made plan with AddDirs set passes, although the spec says ANY flag is refused; deviation 58 records this.
S5.5.4 does not check that the rootless home is named kh-<10 hex>; it checks only that its parent is 'own' under a coai-check-* folder.

summary: The planner arm (no flags, a copy for disk, an empty folder for none, web refused), the three seed rows with correct cells, sections and version, the vectors, Runtimes, the generated table and KimiConsultant's flag refusal match the spec, and all 12 scenarios are present and pass with no new failures. The main problem is scope: the shared unconfined caveat sentence for all runtimes was rewritten in both halves without a recorded deviation; the other findings are minor (a wrong R2 citation, a model-attribution mismatch in the status, a redundant vector test and a copied stand-in).
